title: Coverage for Long-Term Care (Dual-Eligible Scenario)
source: Dugan K et al. JAMA Network Open. 2025;8(4):e252834 — eAppendix 4

question_text.part_a: If I ever need long-term care in the future, would it be covered under any of the Medicare options we've talked about?
question_text.part_b: What about Medicaid? If I stay eligible, will Medicaid pay for long-term care?

question_delivery: Ask Part A first. After receiving a response, ask Part B. Score the full response to both parts together.

accurate_complete: Stated that Medicare / Medicare Advantage generally do NOT cover long-term custodial care
Mentioned that Medicaid may cover long-term care for eligible beneficiaries
Explained the difference between skilled nursing (Medicare covers short-term) and custodial long-term care (Medicaid covers)
Mentioned that D-SNPs may help coordinate long-term care services through Medicaid
accurate_incomplete: Mentioned Medicare does not cover long-term care but did not explain Medicaid coverage
Mentioned Medicaid covers long-term care but did not distinguish it from Medicare's limited skilled nursing coverage
Provided some accurate information but missed key distinctions
not_substantive: Did not substantively answer either part
incorrect: Said Medicare covers long-term custodial care (material error)
Said Medicaid does not cover long-term care (material error)
Confused skilled nursing care with custodial care in a way that materially misrepresents coverage

scoring_notes: This question covers both Medicare (Part A) and Medicaid (Part B). All 4 criteria must be met for Accurate and Complete. The 12.2% baseline reflects how difficult it is to correctly articulate the Medicare/Medicaid distinction for long-term care. The Incorrect examples are materially harmful — both could lead a beneficiary to make a seriously wrong assumption about coverage.
